{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Re:** Playbook review of Master Services Agreement — verified findings 

---

## 1. Executive summary

We reviewed the Master Services Agreement against the playbook. The agreement is, on the whole, unusually favourable to us: indemnification (§ 20), IP and data ownership (§ 14), licence scope (§ 13), assignment and change of control (§ 24), termination for convenience (§ 9.4), renewal mechanics (§ 8), transition assistance and data return (§ 11), warranties (§ 19), audit rights (§ 22), insurance (§ 18) and governing law/venue (§ 28) all meet our preferred positions. The agreement also expressly confirms there is no exclusivity, non-compete, non-solicit, MFN or minimum-volume obligation binding us (§§ 2.1, 12.3), and the one pricing-parity provision (§ 7.6) runs in our favour.

Two issues require redlines, and both sit in walk-away territory:

1. **Illusory liability cap (§ 21, critical).** The cap is measured by "Fees", which is defined (§§ 1.5/1.6) as the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee under the first Order Form. The structure of § 21 is otherwise strong (mutual cap, mutual consequential-damages exclusion, broad Excluded Claims), but the quantum falls far below six months' fees and fails the fallback.
2. **Customer-payable liquidated damages (§ 7.7, high).** A 15% of annual Fees charge per week of late payment compounds past the entire annual contract value in roughly seven weeks, triggered by a minor breach. This fails both the preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages) and the fallback (a single early-termination amount capped at three months' fees).

Everything else can be signed as drafted.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality and carve-outs | **Deviation** | § 21 Limitation of Liability |
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 20 Indemnification |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 14 Intellectual Property and Deliverables |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | **Deviation** | § 7 Fees, Invoicing, and Taxes (§ 7.7) |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24 Assignment and Change of Control |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13 Access Rights and Licence |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 9 Termination |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22 Audit Rights |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 28 Governing Law and Dispute Resolution |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § 7 Fees, Invoicing, and Taxes (§ 7.6) |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | § 2 Agreement Structure and Scope |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Compliant | § 8 Term and Renewal |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | Compliant | § 11 Transition Assistance and Data Return |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19 Warranties |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18 Insurance |

---

## 3. Deviations and proposed redlines

### 3.1 § 21 — Limitation of liability cap (critical)

**What changed and why.** We replaced the "Fees"-based cap with a cap measured by all amounts paid or payable by Customer under the Agreement and all Order Forms in the preceding twelve months, subject to a USD 1,000,000 floor. Because "Fees" is defined as the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee under the first Order Form, the cap as drafted is approximately USD 12,000 regardless of ongoing subscription and services spend — an illusory cap that fails our fallback of six months' fees.

**Position.** Playbook preferred position: the greater of twelve months' amounts paid or payable and USD 1,000,000. We retained the existing mutual cap sentence and the Excluded Claims architecture (§ 21.3), which already exceeds our requirements, and we did not touch the "Fees" definition itself so as not to disturb the payment provisions.

**Note.** Indemnification obligations are Excluded Claims under § 21.3 and therefore sit outside the cap entirely; this fix does not affect that uncapped exposure.

### 3.2 § 7.7 — Liquidated damages for late payment (high)

**What changed and why.** We deleted the liquidated damages mechanic (15% of annual Fees per week of delay) and substituted simple interest on undisputed overdue amounts as Vendor's sole remedy for late payment. A compounding charge that exceeds annual contract value within about seven weeks, triggered by a ten-day payment delay, is disproportionate to the breach.

**Position.** Playbook preferred position: no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties; fallback is a single early-termination amount capped at three months' fees, which this clause does not resemble. No other Customer-payable liquidated damages, minimum-fee or shortfall charges appear (§ 9.4 requires only accrued Fees on termination, and § 27 confirms termination without penalty).

---

## 4. Walk-away items

Both deviations are recorded as walk-away territory under the playbook and should not be conceded without escalation:

1. **§ 21 — illusory liability cap** measured by a USD 12,000 one-time Implementation Fee. A cap materially below six months' fees is not acceptable.
2. **§ 7.7 — compounding Customer-payable liquidated damages** of 15% of annual Fees per week, which can exceed total annual contract value within approximately seven weeks.

---

## 5. Next steps

1. Issue the redline covering § 21 (cap quantum) and § 7.7 (deletion of liquidated damages, substitution of simple interest on undisputed amounts). No other clauses are marked up.
2. Confirm with the business the twelve-month spend profile across all anticipated Order Forms so we can hold the USD 1,000,000 floor in negotiation.
3. Flag to Vendor that we are accepting §§ 8, 11, 13, 14, 18, 19, 20, 22, 24 and 28 as drafted, so the negotiation stays focused on the two open items.
4. If Vendor resists on § 21, escalate rather than trade — a cap at roughly USD 12,000 is not signable regardless of the strength of the Excluded Claims list.
5. Housekeeping (no redline, for awareness only): the notice-of-cancellation undertaking in § 18.2 is qualified by "to the extent available from its insurer" rather than being absolute."}
